title: fix(cli): one verdict sentence for the nine CLI-owned rule ids and the undeclared-handlers boot line; the reasoning moves behind `os explain`
body:
Fixes #22841
Clause-②: no

The `domain:cli` half of the one-line-verdict work: the nine rule ids `packages/cli` produces now print one verdict sentence of at most 200 characters, `os explain RULE_ID` carries the reasoning they used to print, and the undeclared-handlers `[action-governance]` boot line is one line. Rule ids, severities, paths, boot-line levels and payloads, and accept/refuse behaviour are unchanged.

## What changed

- **`packages/cli/src/lint/hook-body-lowering.ts`** (`os lint`): the four `hook-body/*` messages are one sentence each, and their remedy moves to the finding's `fix` (printed as `→ fix:` under `--fix`, carried as `fix` in `--json`). The not-lowerable remedy is still chosen per case: inline a module-scope name, or, for a host-only global such as `Intl`, a string handler ref or a validation rule. `hook-body/bundled-fallback` quotes the extractor's own verdict clause, the first line of its refusal up to its first ` — ` or full stop, without the `[hook-body-extract] ORIGIN: ` lead the finding's subject already carries. A word-boundary bound marks any further cut with `…`. `os build` still prints the whole refusal line for every bundled handler, and `--strict-body` prints the full diagnostic.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts`** (`os build`, `os validate`, `os lint`): the four `docs/*` messages are one sentence ending in the remedy. A `DocIssue` has no separate fix channel, so the remedy stays in the sentence. A message no longer repeats the finding's `path`, because every printer already leads with it. Lists of files, packages and directories quote the first three and count the rest; the `tags:` spelling a doc wrote is quoted up to 48 characters.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`**: the `picklist-reference-unverified` notice is one sentence and quotes at most two outside dependencies. Its `hint` is unchanged.
- **`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`**: nine new `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` entries, one per id, in a section for the ids the CLI produces. ⛔ No existing entry changed: the only removed lines are two lines of the module header, which now names the CLI ids' holding test. No second registry.
- **`packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts`**: the undeclared-handlers line is one line of 192 characters (was 628). It keeps naming the three sources it read and states the 404 as expected, not measured. The ADR-0110 D3 citation and the "if it IS declared, report it rather than dropping a registration that may be serving traffic" branch move into the source comment at the call site: a boot-log line has no rule id, so it has no `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` key. The dead-button line is unchanged (163 characters, already `STATEMENT; FIX`), so `ACTIONABLE_BOOT_CLASSES` in `format.ts` needs no change.

## Census, before → after

Every finding the CLI's suites fire, through a scratch `--import` preload that patches `Array.prototype.push` and records each finding-shaped object whose `rule` is one of the nine. Ten files ran: `hook-body-lowering`, `lint-hook-rules-reach-handler-hooks`, `lint-handwritten-checks-package-fold`, the four `collect-docs*`, `picklist-references`, `picklist-reference-doors` and `explain-rule-id`. Messages are deduped per process and counted by message length.

- BEFORE: the three producers restored from `45e206e498` into the working tree only, each proven equal to its BASE blob by hash. After the run they were restored to HEAD (blob = HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty).
- AFTER: `d6c01cf32c`; the three producers' blobs are identical at the final head.

| rule id | producer | severity | before: n · chars | after: n · chars | fix (after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hook-body/not-lowerable` | `lint/hook-body-lowering.ts` | error | 8 · 565–661 | 8 · 165–178 | ≤ 152 |
| `hook-body/bundled-fallback` | `lint/hook-body-lowering.ts` | warning | 6 · 324–947 | 6 · 109–171 | 142 |
| `hook-body/unparseable` | `lint/hook-body-lowering.ts` | warning | 2 · 469 | 2 · 157 | 101 |
| `hook-body/extraction-failed` | `lint/hook-body-lowering.ts` | warning | 2 · 331 | 2 · 140 | 111 |
| `docs/uncollected-directory` | `utils/collect-docs.ts` | warning | 19 · 433–558 | 17 · 124–183 | (in the sentence) |
| `docs/duplicate-name` | `utils/collect-docs.ts` | error | 3 · 101–330 | 3 · 101–167 | (in the sentence) |
| `docs/nav-target` | `utils/collect-docs.ts` | error | 10 · 263–299 | 9 · 147–184 | (in the sentence) |
| `docs/frontmatter-tags` | `utils/collect-docs.ts` | warning | 5 · 233–285 | 5 · 135–195 | (in the sentence) |
| `picklist-reference-unverified` | `utils/picklist-references.ts` | info | 5 · 240–245 | 5 · 173–175 | hint 125, unchanged |

Rows over 200 after: **0**. Fewer distinct messages after for two ids because shortened messages that no longer repeat the path collapse to the same text.

**Every refusal the extractor can throw** (the extractor is unchanged from `45e206e498`, and today's extractor PRs are on `main`). I built one hook per refusal, with `toString` pinned to its source: 14 forbidden constructs and 7 parameter refusals. Each ran under a short hook name and a 43-character one, through the BASE `hook-body-lowering.ts` and the HEAD one. `hook-body/bundled-fallback` went from 296–1,011 to 113–199, with 0 over 200. The 14 forbidden constructs cut cleanly at the verdict clause (e.g. `` hook 'enrich_lead' is bundled, not shipped as a metadata-only body: `ctx.dispatch.scope` is not reachable from a sandboxed body ``). `require()` and the parameter refusals reach the bound and end in `…`, still naming the construct.

**`[action-governance]`** (message string, without the logger prefix and the JSON `count`/`handlers` tail; the dispatch's "about 790" is the printed record): undeclared handlers 628 → 192; unbound declarations 163 → 163 (unchanged).

## Where `os explain` reads these entries, and the coverage check

`rule-explanations.test.ts` holds every key to a string constant the `@objectstack/lint` root barrel exports, or to `FUNCTIONAL_COMPLETENESS_RULES`, which it imports from the producing package. It would refuse the nine CLI ids. `@objectstack/lint` cannot import `@objectstack/cli`, which depends on it. So the check is extended rather than weakened, in two halves:

- the lint test declares the nine ids as an exact list: a key that is neither a lint id nor listed fails, and so does a listed id with no entry;
- a new block in `packages/cli/test/explain-rule-id.test.ts` fires each of the nine from its real producer. It holds the fired set equal to the explained ids no lint rule produces, and holds each verdict and each fix to one line of at most 200 characters. It also checks that each `rule:` pointer names its entry.

## Verification (final head `baa4d20e8b`, which merges `origin/main` `63739521d8`)

Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, with each part's exit captured in its own log.

- `@objectstack/lint`: typecheck exit 0 (test layer OK; `--listFiles` counts `rule-explanations.test.ts` once); `vitest run`: Test Files 137 passed (137), Tests 6498 passed (6498).
- `@objectstack/objectql`: typecheck exit 0; `vitest run --project local`: Test Files 401 passed (401), Tests 7817 passed (7817).
- `@objectstack/cli`: typecheck exit 0 (`--listFiles`: `test/explain-rule-id.test.ts` in `tsconfig.test.json`; both touched `src/` tests in `tsconfig.json`); `vitest run --project unit`: Test Files 283 passed (283), Tests 4267 passed (4267). The `integration` tier is declared to CI. The one integration file naming these ids, `test/picklist-reference-doors.test.ts`, ran: 1 file, 11 tests.
- Readers of the boot lines: objectql's five files naming them (5 files, 59 tests, run at `ab2394a6db`; all inside the full objectql run above), `packages/runtime/src/action-governance-scope-divergence.test.ts` (1 / 6), and cli `format.boot-warning-classes` + `boot-log-capture` (2 / 34).
- Nightly-tier e2e files naming these ids or the `[action-governance]` lines (`OS_TEST_TIERS=nightly`): `build-json-advisory-parity`, `build-json-failure-warnings`, `validate-json-failure-warnings`, `rule-line-explain-pointer`, `serve-boot-diagnostics-noise-budget`, `serve-boot-diagnostics`, `serve-app-runtime-hooks`: Test Files 7 passed (7), Tests 37 passed (37).
- **Reverse verification:** the BEFORE census leg ran the edited suites against the BASE producers. Predicted exactly four red, the four text pins this PR moves; observed exactly those four (190 tests, 4 failed). At HEAD all 190 pass.
- **Ablation of the new 200-character bound**, from committed `ab2394a6db`, via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` plus a shell trap restoring HEAD by absolute path. I put `docs/nav-target`'s old remedy sentence back (anchor ×1 → ×0, blob `f9b2cc6775` → `5b83912577`). Predicted exactly one red, the bound pin, because the nav-target suite's own pins still match. Observed `Tests 1 failed | 21 passed (22)`, the bound pin reading 264. Restored to blob `f9b2cc6775` = HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- ESLint, narrowed and proven: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 9 changed `.ts` files reports 9 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The population is from `eslint.config.mjs` (`**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` plus the `packages/**` blocks). The config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so no untouched file's verdict can move.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` with no paths, at `baa4d20e8b`, derives 69: the dispatch's 62, plus `check:cli-test-child-env`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:objectql-double-limit`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt` and `check:where-matcher`, which the touched test files pull in. They ran sequentially, one log each, exit captured before any pipe. 66 exited 0 on the first pass. Three refused on a prerequisite and exited 0 once it was met:
  - `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90` (exit 2, shallow clone): passed after `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-06`;
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, package dists absent): passed after `check:type-check-debt --re-measure`, later in the same run, built them. `check-i18n-coverage: OK (13 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`.

  `--ran`: `Run reconciliation — 69 derived, 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.` CI was not awaited.

## Acceptance notes

- **The other mentions of these ids are not producers.** `docs/duplicate-name` in `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts` and `docs/nav-target` in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts` (and `app-doc-nav-item.test.ts`, `meta-app-nav-doc-audience.test.ts`) all sit in doc comments; the only producers are the three CLI files above.
- **No pointer on two printers' `rule:` lines.** `os build` and `os validate` print a doc finding's `rule:` line (`printDocIssueErrors` in `format.ts`, the doc-warning loop in `compile.ts`, the warning list in `validate.ts`), and the picklist notice printer prints `[rule] message` with `→ hint`. Neither appends `explainPointer`, so the new entries are reached through `os explain RULE_ID` and its listing, and `os lint`'s `rule:` line, which does print the pointer. A doc finding also has no `fix` channel. Both are printer changes outside this card's file surface; carrier: none.
- **The bundled-fallback verdict reads the extractor's prose.** It takes the first clause of the refusal line, so a structured short reason on `HookBodyExtractionError` (`extract-hook-body.ts`, the producer) would remove that cut. Not a defect today: every current refusal is measured above; carrier: none.
- **A third `[action-governance]` line**, the inventory-SKIPPED notice in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, is 482 characters. It is not one of the two lines this card names, and still says "REFUSED at dispatch", which the inventory line itself was earlier corrected to stop asserting; carrier: none.
- `picklist-reference-unknown`, the refusal beside `picklist-reference-unverified` and not one of the nine, quotes up to ten declared lists. With ten long names it can pass 200 characters (333 on a constructed input; not measured on a fired finding).
- The card body places the `hook-body/*` messages in `extract-hook-body.ts`; they are composed in `hook-body-lowering.ts`, as the seat's note on the card already says.
- NOT MEASURED: whether `objectstack-ai/objectui` matches any of these texts. Code search is refused in this session (repo-scoped). These are CLI terminal and server boot-log texts, and the changeset says to match on `rule` and `path`.
